item.title: #3592330: Workspaces PR 24: lock a Canvas config draft to one workspace, the same way as content
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +363/−30 · php +359/−28 · md +4/−2
  • Diff: 5cf2fda
  • Discussion: #3592330 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

On the unreleased 1.x-workspaces branch, a Canvas config entity (content template, pattern, page variant, code component and so on) with a draft in one workspace is now locked to that workspace, the same way content is. A second workspace, Main included, that tries to write a draft of the same entity is refused with a 409 naming the owner, until the draft is published or discarded. This stops the workspace published last from silently overwriting the other's config change in Live. A staged translation of a config entity shares its entity's lock, so a draft of either one locks both.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

WorkspaceAutoSave::getFallbackDraftOwningWorkspaceId() finds the owner of a config entity by looking for a row in each workspace's AutoSaveFallbackStore collection, skipping the staging workspace. The fallback row is the lock, not the draft marker, since staged config translations and rows migrated from 1.x have no marker.

The lock is a group: the config entity plus its StagedLanguageConfigOverride drafts, one key per site language, built as staged_language_config_override:<langcode>.<config name>. A staged translation resolves its parent through ConfigManagerInterface::loadConfigEntityByName(); a ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase uses getConfigDependencyName(). Without grouping, a workspace could stage the parent and then be refused on a translation the other workspace holds, leaving a partial draft. WorkspaceAutoSave now takes ConfigManagerInterface and LanguageManagerInterface in its constructor, and AutoSaveFallbackStore::getDrafts() is new, returning the drafts for a list of keys in one call. holdsLockGroupDraft() uses it per workspace.

Because one workspace can hold a draft of the group at a time, the publish-time hash-advance comment in AutoSaveManager was reworded: a draft in another workspace is only possible for a Live save of the translation made outside a publish. ADR 0022 decision 5 was updated to say translations share the lock. The editor shows no lock notice for config; the second editor just sees the 409 (EntityLockedInAnotherWorkspace, with the owner in meta.workspace). New tests cover the layout PATCH 409 body for a content template and the lock in both directions between a parent and its fr translation draft.

item.title: #3592283: Brand Kit – UX Improvements
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +285/−275 · js +280/−249 · css +5/−26
  • Diff: 6fc7814
  • Discussion: #3592283 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Three Brand Kit color UX tweaks in Canvas. Deleting a color now opens a centered confirmation dialog, matching folder deletion, instead of a popover anchored to the row. When editing a color, Save stays disabled and the "this will affect N components" usage notice stays hidden until the color value or CSS variable name actually changes. New Color props in the code editor now default to white instead of red.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The popover DeleteColorPopover (and its CSS module) was removed and replaced by DeleteColorDialog, built on the shared Dialog component and mounted in the app's Dialogs list. It is driven by a new deleteColorConfirm entry in dialogSlice (DialogDataMap), which ColorRow opens via setDialogWithDataOpen with the color as data, closing the edit popover first. The usage/blocked/prior-version messaging and useDeleteColorMutation logic are carried over unchanged. The shared Dialog buttons gained data-testid attributes dialog-cancel-button and dialog-confirm-button.

In ColorFormPopover, the form state now tracks originalVariableName. A hasChanges flag compares the current variable name with the original and compares the color space, components and alpha against originalColor. In edit mode isConfirmDisabled also requires hasChanges, and the usage info box is rendered only when hasChanges is true. The info text gained data-testid="color-variable-edit-info".

The default color example for the Color prop type changed from #ff0000ff to #ffffff in the derived prop types, and FALLBACK_DEFAULT_COLOR in the color prop field changed to match.

item.title: #3592263: Workspaces PR 15: staged drafts are invisible to the Workspaces API and the Workspaces UI
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 29 files, +1543/−81 · php +1514/−70 · md +25/−11 · neon +2 · yml +1 · json +1
  • Diff: b93ef97
  • Discussion: #3592263 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

Canvas config drafts (content templates, patterns, page variants, code components) were invisible to core's Workspaces screens, because core only tracks content entity revisions. A workspace holding only config drafts showed "no changes" on the publish and manage pages, the Publish button was disabled, and the delete form did not name the drafts it would discard. Each config draft now has a small tracked "Canvas draft" marker, so core lists and counts it (for example "1 Canvas draft"). Run database updates after upgrading. Drafts that already exist get a marker only on their next auto-save.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: canvas_update_11203() installs the new canvas_auto_save_draft_marker content entity type.
  • Config change: None beyond the new entity type; the Doctor JSON schema gains an auto_save_draft_markers entry.
  • New API: Internal AutoSaveDraftMarker entity, AutoSaveDraftMarkerManager service, and new auto_save_draft_markers Doctor check (advisory risk).

Technical details

Config drafts stay as rows in the per-workspace fallback store; a new internal, revisionable content entity type canvas_auto_save_draft_marker (Drupal\canvas\Entity\AutoSaveDraftMarker, using core's DefaultWorkspaceHandler) is tracked by WorkspaceTracker in their place. Decorating the tracker was rejected because its consumers pass the returned revision IDs to loadMultipleRevisions() or deleteRevision(), which config entities cannot satisfy. The marker stores the workspace ID, fallback key, target entity type and ID, and langcode; label, changed time and owner are read from the store's metadata at render time, so later auto-saves write no new revision.

The new AutoSaveDraftMarkerManager service creates the marker inside the workspace on the first fallback-store write and deletes it outside any workspace on discard, after publish, and on workspace delete. A unique key on the target is added through AutoSaveDraftMarkerStorageSchema. AutoSaveManager::purgeDeletedEntity() ignores markers. The new auto_save_draft_markers Doctor check reports drafts without a marker and markers without a draft as an advisory risk, not a failure. ADR 0022 is updated accordingly.

The commit also changes publish gating. AutoSaveManager::hasChangedLiveBase() makes the pre-publish check refuse a config draft whose Live entity changed since the draft started (reusing the base hash comparison extracted into getChangedLiveBase()), and a new onCanvasConfigOverrideChange() subscriber on language.save_override and language.delete_override advances a draft's stored base hash when its entity gains or loses a translation. Per the issue, WorkspacePublishValidationException is changed to extend core's WorkspacePublishException, so the publish form shows per-item violations; that file was in the omitted part of the diff and I did not read it. Merging child workspaces is explicitly not supported; ADR 0022 records this.

Upgrade

Run drush updatedb. canvas_update_11203() installs the canvas_auto_save_draft_marker entity type. Existing config drafts are not backfilled (see the @todo Workspaces MR 6 in the update function) and get a marker on their next auto-save.

item.title: #3592386: Canvas AI: Cannot create code components outside of canvas pages
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +62/−22 · php +62/−22
  • Diff: ac552df
  • Discussion: #3592386 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

In Canvas 1.x, asking Canvas AI to create a code component from /canvas failed with "Unable to read the page layout. Please reload the page and try again." because the AI request was rejected whenever the editor sent no page layout regions. That blanket check is removed, so code component requests now go through. Agents that really need page regions now report a missing layout themselves.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In CanvasAiLegacyBuilder, the early return for an empty current_layout.regions is removed. The layout is now written to CanvasAiTempStore under CURRENT_LAYOUT_KEY only when regions exist. Otherwise the key is deleted with deleteData(), so a layout left from an earlier request can't leak into a request without one.

The region check moved to where regions are actually needed: CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper::validateRegionExists() returns a message when the layout has no regions at all ("Unable to read the page layout: no regions were sent. Do not retry; tell the user to reload the page and try again."). Previously that case produced the misleading "Region ... does not exist" text. Kernel tests in CanvasAiBuilderControllerTest now assert the controller doesn't refuse such requests and that only a layout with regions is stored, and a new testValidateRegionExists covers the helper.

item.title: #3592223: Canvas AI: Include a skill for page creation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +364/−0 · md +364
  • Diff: fb22f94
  • Discussion: #3592223 · 1 contributor · 26 comments

Summary

Canvas AI now ships a skill for coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex. You build a few pages by hand in Canvas and give the skill their IDs. It studies them and writes a page guideline: which component trees serve each kind of section, typical section order, and which backgrounds, text and button styles go together. Saved as an AI Context item, the guideline helps the Canvas page agent build new pages that match the rest of the site. It also has a refine step for when a generated page comes out wrong.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New agent skill canvas-ai-page-context-generation under modules/canvas_ai/.agents/skills/ that generates a page guideline Markdown file for the Canvas page agent.

Technical details

The skill lives in modules/canvas_ai/.agents/skills/canvas-ai-page-context-generation/ as SKILL.md, a README.md, references/output-format.md and references/refine.md. It only reads the site through Drush. For page structure it loads the Page entity (using the auto-save entity when there are unpublished changes) and dumps each component's inputs as YAML. For what the page agent sees it calls canvas_ai.component_context_helper (getComponentCatalog() and getComponentDetails()), so every component ID, prop, enum value and slot written into the guideline is checked against what the agent receives. Components on pages but missing from the catalog are reported rather than written into trees.

The output is a file in canvas-page-guidelines/ (default site.md) with front matter (label, description, purpose) and one YAML block. The YAML covers structure, rules, colors, spacing, rich_text, typography, copy, an index of patterns by content purpose, and patterns with look, vary, repeat ranges and component trees. The document is limited to about 10,000 tokens. The skill offers, step by step and only with the user's agreement, to check the canvas_ai_context recipe consumer config, create or update an ai_context_item, and raise ai_context.settings max_tokens. It does not change the site otherwise.

Upgrade

To use it, copy the skill into your coding agent's skills directory in the project root (for Claude Code):

mkdir -p .claude/skills
cp -R web/modules/contrib/canvas/modules/canvas_ai/.agents/skills/canvas-ai-page-context-generation .claude/skills/

Using the guideline needs the AI Context module connected to the page agent via the canvas_ai_context recipe, and roles using Canvas AI need the access published ai context permission.

item.title: #3592397: Limit the creation of exposed slots to only Node
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +116/−18 · php +81/−1 · js +29/−14 · yml +3/−1 · mdx +2/−1 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 385d9a8
  • Discussion: #3592397 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

Canvas content templates can now be created for entity types other than nodes, which accidentally made the new exposed slots feature available for them too. Exposed slots are now limited to node content templates in the full view mode. In the editor, the "Enable editing" option for slots is disabled on templates for other entity types, and the API and config validation reject exposed slots on them.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: exposed_slots in canvas.content_template.*.*.* now validates that the template's entity type is node (new entityTypeId option on ValidExposedSlot).

Technical details

ValidExposedSlotConstraint gets a new entityTypeId option (default EXPOSED_SLOTS_ENTITY_TYPE_ID, node) and an entityTypeMismatchMessage. It is set next to viewMode: full in the canvas.content_template.*.*.* config schema. ValidExposedSlotConstraintValidator compares ContentTemplate::getTargetEntityTypeId() against it and adds a violation before checking the component tree.

ApiContentTemplateSlotFieldController::create() (the slot-fields endpoint that creates canvas_slot_ fields) now throws a 422 UnprocessableEntityHttpException with Exposed slots are only allowed for the node entity type. for non-node templates, before the existing view mode check, so no field is created.

On the UI side, a new EXPOSED_SLOTS_ENTITY_TYPE_ID constant mirrors the PHP one. SlotExposePanel and SlotMenuItems now also read entityType from the route params and disable "Enable editing" unless both entity type and view mode match. The docs and canvas.content_template schema comments were updated accordingly. Tests cover config validation and the HTTP API for a user template.

item.title: #3592163: Canvas AI: Deprecate existing agents and switch to client-side orchestration
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 72 files, +2092/−1842 · php +1912/−1736 · js +74/−40 · yml +72/−65 · md +34/−1
  • Diff: 40ce774
  • Discussion: #3592163 · 1 contributor · 42 comments

Summary

Canvas AI now ships the new client-side orchestrated chat and is no longer hidden, so it can be enabled normally. New sites get the new chat when they install Canvas AI. Existing sites that already have Canvas AI get a new deprecated module, canvas_ai_legacy, installed by the update. It holds the old orchestrator agents and tools, so the existing chat keeps working with any customizations kept. While it is installed, the chat shows a legacy warning that links to the change record (#3628747), and the deprecated agents' edit forms show a deprecation warning. To switch to the new chat, uninstall canvas_ai_legacy. This deletes the five legacy agents, including any changes made to them. On sites that deploy configuration, export after the updates and again after uninstalling.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: canvas_ai_update_11200() installs canvas_ai_legacy; post-updates 0015 and 0016 set legacy agent dependencies and install the new agents and settings.
  • Config change: main_agent, tools and keep_tool_calls_in_history move from canvas_dev_ai.settings to canvas_ai.settings; canvas_agent and drupal_canvas_page_agent now ship in canvas_ai/config/install; the five legacy agents are now enforced on canvas_ai_legacy.
  • API change: Route canvas_ai.canvas_builder renamed to canvas_ai.builder; route canvas_ai.get_progress removed from canvas_ai (now canvas_ai_legacy.get_progress at /admin/api/canvas/ai-progress-legacy); token [canvas_dev_ai:available_tools] is now [canvas_ai:available_tools].
  • Deprecation: The orchestrator-based Canvas AI agents (canvas_ai_orchestrator, canvas_page_builder_agent, canvas_template_builder_agent, canvas_title_generation_agent, canvas_metadata_generation_agent) are deprecated and moved to canvas_ai_legacy.
  • New API: New deprecated module canvas_ai_legacy with route /admin/api/canvas/ai-legacy; new Agents & Tools form at /admin/config/ai/canvas-ai-agent-selection in Canvas AI.

Technical details

The code that was in the hidden canvas_dev_ai module moved into canvas_ai: the canvas_agent and drupal_canvas_page_agent agents (in config/install, enforced on canvas_ai), the main_agent, tools and keep_tool_calls_in_history settings (now in canvas_ai.settings with schema), the CanvasAiAgentSelectionForm as an "Agents & Tools" tab, and the chat controller, which is merged into CanvasBuilder at /admin/api/canvas/ai. canvas_ai_install() sets main_agent and tools in code rather than in config/install, because simple config is saved before the module's config entities exist and the ConfigExists constraints would fail (see core #3425992). canvas_dev_ai is left only to set the aiDevMode flag.

The legacy chat controller is now CanvasAiLegacyBuilder in canvas_ai_legacy, serving /admin/api/canvas/ai-legacy and /admin/api/canvas/ai-progress-legacy. The legacy agents are in that module's config/optional, with their enforced module dependency changed from canvas_ai to canvas_ai_legacy, so uninstalling the module removes them. Existing canvas_ai post-updates that reimport agent config now read from canvas_ai_legacy/config/optional. canvas_component_agent stays in Canvas AI because the new chat uses it too. The legacy UI code (AiWizard.tsx) stays in the Canvas UI package. While canvas_ai_legacy is installed, the new agents installed by post-update 0016 have no effect.

The diff shown was partial (40 of 72 files), so the controller merge and the UI changes were not read in full.

Upgrade

Existing sites run the updates; no manual step is needed to keep the legacy chat:

drush updb

This runs canvas_ai_update_11200(), which installs canvas_ai_legacy, then post-updates canvas_ai_post_update_0015_enforce_legacy_agent_dependency() and canvas_ai_post_update_0016_install_chat_agents().

To switch to the new chat (this deletes the five legacy agents):

drush pm:uninstall canvas_ai_legacy

Custom code or config that references canvas_dev_ai.settings, the [canvas_dev_ai:available_tools] token, or the route canvas_ai.canvas_builder or canvas_ai.get_progress must be updated to canvas_ai.settings, [canvas_ai:available_tools], canvas_ai.builder, or canvas_ai_legacy.get_progress.

item.title: #3592391: Workspaces PR 28: in a workspace the user can view, the Canvas API refuses reads and content writes that core allows
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +41/−47 · php +41/−47
  • Diff: 4613e30
  • Discussion: #3592391 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, a user who can view a workspace but not edit it can now use the Canvas editor in that workspace. Before, they could switch to it, but the Canvas API returned 403 for reads, so the page list and page selector failed to load. Writes into the workspace are now decided by normal content access, the same as core's entity forms, not by permission to edit the workspace itself.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Permission change: Canvas API requests in a named workspace no longer require edit own workspace / edit any workspace; view access to the workspace plus content entity permissions is enough.

Technical details

WorkspaceRequestSubscriber::onRequest() had a check that threw AccessDeniedHttpException unless the active workspace granted update to the current user. In core, update on a workspace means edit own workspace / edit any workspace. That permission covers the workspace entity and publishing it, not the content inside it. The canvas_requires_workspace route option made the check run on GET requests too, which caused the 403s. The check is removed. The header required check (400), the header and active workspace mismatch (409) and the live handling are unchanged. No view check replaces it, because core's WorkspaceManager::getActiveWorkspace() already falls back to Live when the user lacks view.

The now-unused $currentUser constructor argument and the AccessDeniedHttpException import are removed from the subscriber. Publishing a workspace still goes through the canvas.api.workspaces.* routes, which the subscriber skips, and still needs the core edit permissions. In ApiAutoSaveControllerTest, testNamedWorkspaceWritesNeedUpdateAccess() became testNamedWorkspaceViewerUsesCanvasApi(). It asserts that a viewer can list, stage and discard, and that a user without entity access is refused with a 403 from entity access.

item.title: #3592390: canvas_oauth should automatically create the CLI user, and consumer, upon installation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +267/−2 · php +134/−2 · yml +124 · md +9
  • Diff: 308f459
  • Discussion: #3592390 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Canvas OAuth now ships a recipe, cli_setup, that does most of the Canvas CLI OAuth setup for you. It installs canvas_oauth and media, creates a "Canvas CLI" user and a cli OAuth consumer with all Canvas scopes, and creates the media scopes for existing media types. The README now lists this as the recommended route, with the previous manual steps kept as an alternative.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New createOAuthScope config action (plugin CreateOAuthScope) for media_type config entities; MediaScopesHelper::ensureMediaScopes() now accepts an optional list of media type IDs.

Technical details

The recipe lives in modules/canvas_oauth/recipes/cli_setup. It imports canvas_oauth config and ships two default content entities with hard-coded UUIDs: a user (72810686-42f1-43cf-80fa-8a35a7cb5a08) and a consumer (9a1724a1-6a79-4819-87e3-871542db531b) that depends on that user. The consumer uses the client_credentials grant, is confidential, and lists the 13 Canvas scopes (page, media, brand kit, JS component and so on). Applying the recipe again should not duplicate them, because the UUIDs are fixed. Both are content entities, so they have to be shipped as recipe content rather than config.

Media scopes depend on which media types exist, so they cannot be listed statically. The recipe instead runs a new createOAuthScope config action against media.type.*. The action is implemented by Drupal\canvas_oauth\Plugin\ConfigAction\CreateOAuthScope, which calls MediaScopesHelper::ensureMediaScopes(). That method gained an optional ?array $media_types parameter, so the action can create scopes for one media type at a time. With NULL it still processes all media types. CliSetupRecipeTest checks that image and document types get scopes, that a media type with a non-file source (test) does not, and that the consumer ends up with every canvas_ scope.

Upgrade

Apply the recipe from the command line:

dr recipe modules/contrib/canvas/modules/canvas_oauth/recipes/cli_setup

item.title: #3592387: Workspaces PR 27: list, activate and delete only default-provider workspaces and Main in the Canvas workspace API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +120/−5 · php +101/−2 · yml +19/−3
  • Diff: 35011eb
  • Discussion: #3592387 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The Canvas workspace API now only deals with workspaces that belong to the Canvas flow: top-level workspaces of core's default provider, plus Main. Workspaces registered by another module's workspace provider no longer appear in the Canvas workspace switcher, and they can no longer be activated or deleted through Canvas. This matches what core's own workspace UI already does.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ApiWorkspaceController gained a private static isInCanvasFlow() helper. It returns FALSE for sub-workspaces (hasParent()) and for any workspace whose provider field is not DefaultWorkspaceProvider::getId() or CanvasMainWorkspaceProvider::ID. list() skips such workspaces next to the existing view access check, replacing the earlier inline hasParent() check.

activate() and delete() call a new assertInCanvasFlow() before the access checks. It throws a NotFoundHttpException whose previous exception is a ParamNotConvertedException, so the response matches an unknown workspace ID (empty 404 body) and the API does not reveal workspaces it does not list. As a result, sub-workspaces now also get a 404 from activate() and delete(), where before only list() hid them. The OpenAPI descriptions for the three operations were updated. A new test module canvas_test_workspace_provider registers a ForeignWorkspaceProvider, and ApiWorkspaceControllerTest covers the list, activate and delete cases.

item.title: #3592209: `canvas_workflows` sub-module: review workflow and scheduled publish on top of core Workflows
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 58 files, +5412/−173 · php +2828/−16 · js +2005/−142 · yml +397/−4 · md +181/−10 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: fd06947
  • Discussion: #3592209 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas gains an optional canvas_workflows sub-module that adds a review process to workspaces. Each workspace can be assigned a core Workflows workflow (shipped default: Draft, In review, Approved) and cannot be published, from Canvas, the Workspaces UI or cron, until it reaches an approved state. Approved workspaces can also be scheduled to publish at a set time via cron. Editing an approved workspace sends it back to draft and cancels its schedule. Choosing a workspace's review workflow needs the new administer canvas workspace review permission. Canvas works unchanged without the module installed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New canvas_workspace_review workflow type and default workflow config shipped by the canvas_workflows sub-module.
  • Permission change: New administer canvas workspace review permission, plus generated use {workflow} transition {transition} permissions.
  • New API: New hook_canvas_workspace_staged_write() in Canvas, fired on staged writes and draft discards into a workspace.

Technical details

The sub-module defines a canvas_workspace_review workflow type (WorkspaceReviewWorkflowType) whose states carry an approved_for_publish flag, and ships a default canvas_workspace_review workflow config with submit_for_review, approve and send_back transitions. Each transition gets a generated use {workflow} transition {transition} permission via WorkspaceReviewPermissions. hook_entity_base_field_info() adds base fields to the workspace entity: canvas_review_workflow (empty means no review), canvas_workspace_status, canvas_scheduled_publish_at, canvas_scheduled_publish_by and canvas_scheduled_publish_error. Only workspaces of core's default provider are reviewable; Main and module-created workspaces are not. hook_entity_field_access() forbids edits to every field except canvas_review_workflow, which needs the new permission, because core grants workspace edit and publish through the same permissions. Changing the workflow resets the state and schedule in hook_workspace_presave().

WorkspaceReviewPublishSubscriber listens to WorkspacePrePublishEvent at priority 100 and calls stopPublishing() for a review-required workspace that is not approved, ahead of Canvas's validation subscriber (so a review refusal surfaces as a 409 rather than a 422). On WorkspacePostPublishEvent it clears the state and schedule. item.title: #3591817: Add exposed slots: per-entity editable areas in content templates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 167 files, +14253/−674 · js +6817/−286 · php +6142/−357 · yml +867/−20 · css +203/−3 · mdx +99 · md +79/−5 · json +41 · svg +3/−3 · txt +2
  • Diff: 6c9eea2
  • Discussion: #3591817 · 1 contributor · 27 comments
  • Followers: 3

Summary

Content templates can now have exposed slots: a site builder marks slots in a template as editable per entity, and content creators fill them with their own components on each node, while the rest of the template stays locked. Each exposed slot is backed by its own Canvas (component_tree) field on the content type. A template can expose several slots, and content already placed in a slot acts as the default until an entity overrides it. An override can also be deliberately empty. Removing a slot from the template only detaches it, so entity content is kept and returns if the slot is exposed again. Deleting the field itself happens in Field UI. This last commit adds an "Edit in Canvas" tab on templated nodes and a Content panel in the editor. The panel lists templated entities grouped by content type and is searchable. It also adds end-to-end tests.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: New post-update canvas_post_update_0032_install_empty_slot_marker() installs the marker.empty_slot component on existing sites. Sites using config sync must export config after running it.
  • Config change: ContentTemplate::exposed_slots is now keyed by the machine name of a component_tree field on the template's bundle; the template gains config dependencies on those field configs. New canvas.component.marker.empty_slot config ships (disabled).
  • Permission change: administer content templates is now marked restrict access: true because exposing a slot can create a canvas_slot_* field storage.
  • New API: New routes canvas.api.content_template.slot_field.create|list|usage under /canvas/api/v0/config/content_template/{content_template}/slot-fields, the canvas.content.layout local task, ContentTemplate::getMergedComponentTree(), and exposed_slots in the content template client payload, CLI types and schema.

Technical details

Storage: exposed_slots keys are now machine names of component_tree fields on the template's bundle (validated by ValidExposedSlotConstraintValidator, key pattern now lowercase letters, digits and underscores). Each entry keeps component_uuid, slot_name and label. ContentTemplate::calculateDependencies() adds the field configs as dependencies, and onDependencyRemoval() drops the matching slot when a field is deleted, so a template is not cascade-deleted. preSave() prunes slots whose target component no longer exists. The old assert(count === 1) in ContentTemplate::build() is gone. build() now uses the new getMergedComponentTree(), which calls ComponentTreeItemList::injectSlotContent() (replacing injectSubTreeItemList()) for each slot field. A slot field the user cannot view renders the template default, and a SubtreeInjectionException (for example a UUID collision) is logged and falls back to the default. ExposedSlotContentIsMergeableConstraint validates this on entity save.

Empty overrides: an empty field means "inherit the default". An override that renders nothing is stored as a single marker.empty_slot component instance (new Marker::EMPTY_SLOT_LOCAL_ID, a disabled Component config shipped in config/install), which Component::preSave() keeps disabled.

HTTP/UI: ApiContentTemplateSlotFieldController creates canvas_slot_-prefixed component_tree fields (with symmetric translation sync when content_translation is installed, 409 if the bundle already has the field), lists reusable candidate fields, and reports per-slot override counts. ApiLayoutController serves per-slot editable nodes for templated entities and accepts per-slot subtree writes, and the rest of the template is read-only. ApiContentControllers::list() now also lists entities of bundles with exposed slots (via ComponentTreeLoader::getBundlesWithExposedSlots()). It is gated by _canvas_ui_access plus entity access, and canvas pages still require edit canvas_page. Templated entities only get an edit operation link. The React UI adds Content.tsx/TemplatedContentGroups.tsx, the expose, detach and delete-protection dialogs, slot overlays, and a "Content" contextual-panel tab. The decision is recorded in ADR 0022 (docs/adr/0022-...) and a user guide guides/exposed-slots.mdx. The CLI (packages/cli) pushes exposed_slots and calls createSlotField() before pushing a template.

Upgrade

Existing sites should run database updates so canvas_post_update_0032_install_empty_slot_marker() installs the marker.empty_slot component. If you deploy with config sync, export config afterwards, or the next import removes the marker. The issue states no update hook migrates old data: the earlier test-only storage shape (parent_uuid pointing at a template-internal component UUID) is abandoned, and nothing released stored it. Templates that define exposed_slots by hand must key them by an existing component_tree field on the bundle:

exposed_slots:
  canvas_slot_main:
    label: 'Main'
    component_uuid: <uuid of the component in the template>
    slot_name: <slot name>

item.title: #3591892: Implement json-render in Headless SDK
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 133 files, +7896/−2315 · js +4908/−1772 · php +1743/−340 · json +629/−30 · md +331/−42 · astro +185/−113 · yml +91/−14 · mdx +4/−3 · vue +4/−1 · gitignore +1
  • Diff: c4e025b
  • Discussion: #3591892 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The Canvas Headless content API can now return content in the json-render format when the client sends a Canvas-Client-Capabilities: json-render header. The Headless SDK sends this header automatically and its framework components (React, Astro, Nuxt, Next.js, TanStack Start, Angular) now render json-render through new shared @drupal-canvas/json-render* packages. Clients that do not send the header still get the legacy Custom Elements JSON, which the README says Canvas 2.0.0 will remove. Headless app developers must now pass page.isPreview to the component tree to get preview mode, and the module needs Custom Elements 3.5.0 or later.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: canvas_headless now requires custom_elements 3.5.0 or later.
  • Config change: New canvas_headless_content_format cache context varies content API responses by requested format.
  • API change: Content and entity API accept a Canvas-Client-Capabilities: json-render request header and then return a json-render document (root, elements) instead of nested Custom Elements JSON; CanvasComponentTree gets a preview prop and preview mode is no longer inferred from the tree.
  • New API: New npm packages @drupal-canvas/json-render, -react, -astro, -vue, -angular; new Page.isPreview field from fetchPage(); PHP Drupal\canvas\CanvasClientCapabilities::has().

Technical details

CanvasContentController and CanvasEntityController pick the format with CanvasClientCapabilities::has($request, 'json-render') (case-insensitive, comma-separated tokens) and delegate to the new CanvasContentSerializer. It runs the render array through CanvasRenderConverter, which replaces JsComponentCanvasRenderConverter and is registered as a custom_elements.render_converter at priority 60. It then calls the Custom Elements normalizer, using the new CanvasJsonRenderNormalizer (tagged custom_elements.format_normalizer) for json-render. CanvasCustomElement carries the exact component ID and instance UUID, and keeps authored prop and slot names. Element types keep the component ID, for example js.example_card. Preview responses use canvas-marker, canvas-slot-placeholder and canvas-preview-content-region elements. An empty managed tree is root: "" with elements: {}; unmanaged routes still return content: null. For legacy requests the old single-root and renderless-container shaping is kept inside the serializer.

Caching: the new canvas_headless_content_format cache context (HeadlessContentFormatCacheContext) is added to responses so the two formats are cached separately. CanvasHeadlessServiceProvider alters http_middleware.page_cache to chain a new DisallowCanvasContentApiRequests policy. Only Internal Page Cache is affected, so HTTP caching of public responses is unchanged. openapi.yml documents the header and the CanvasJsonRenderDocument and LegacyCanvasContent schemas.

SDK: the @drupal-canvas/headless package no longer contains its own renderer. Page types now come from @drupal-canvas/json-render, and convertLegacyCustomElementsFormat() (legacy-custom-elements.ts) converts older backend output to json-render using the app's component registry. fetchPage() and the entity fetch return isPreview (live draft session and managed route) instead of marking the tree with canvasDraftMode. The per-framework CanvasComponentTree implementations became thin wrappers over the json-render-* packages. Those packages render the Canvas editor's component, slot and region markers and empty drop targets in preview mode.

Upgrade

Pass the isPreview value from fetchPage() or fetchEntity() to the tree. It is no longer inferred from content.

<CanvasComponentTree
  tree={page.content}
  preview={page.isPreview}
  context={page.context}
  components={{ 'hello-card': HelloCard }}
/>

In Nuxt use :preview="page.isPreview", and in Angular use [preview]="page.isPreview". Update custom_elements to 3.5.0 or later ("drupal/custom_elements": "^3.5.0"). Apps without the SDK header keep receiving legacy Custom Elements JSON until Canvas 2.0.0.

item.title: #3592175: `resolveEntityUri()` hardcodes `entity:node/`, so link props can never target any other entity type
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +639/−18 · php +477 · css +72/−6 · js +46/−12 · yml +44
  • Diff: c691e41
  • Discussion: #3592175 · 1 contributor · 24 comments
  • Followers: 1

Summary

Link props (SDC props with format: uri or uri-reference) can now link to Canvas pages as well as nodes. Previously the autocomplete only matched nodes, and any selection was stored as entity:node/<id>, so picking a Canvas page could silently link to an unrelated node with the same ID. The link autocomplete now returns both nodes and Canvas pages in one list, each row showing the entity's type, and the path on hover.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New canvas.api.ui.link_autocomplete route (/canvas/api/v0/ui/link-autocomplete) served by ApiLinkAutocompleteController, returning {value, label} with the entity type encoded in value.

Technical details

Core's LinkWidget hardcodes #target_type to node (core #2423093), and the issue rejected making it configurable to a single alternative, so Canvas now handles multi-type matching itself.

A new ApiLinkAutocompleteController queries the default selection handler for each of node and canvas_page (exact, STARTS_WITH, then CONTAINS, to avoid weaker matches crowding out better ones), drops entities the user cannot view, ranks results across types (exact, prefix, word prefix, contains, then label), and caps at 10. Each suggestion's value is Label (entity_type_id/entity_id) via encodeValue() (using Tags::encode(), so labels with commas get quoted). The label is markup with a label, path and type pill, styled in css/autocomplete.extend.css.

In ReduxIntegratedFieldWidgetsHooks::fieldWidgetSingleElementLinkDefaultWidgetFormAlter(), when the form is a Canvas static prop source, a processLinkAutocompleteRoute process callback is inserted after EntityAutocomplete::processEntityAutocomplete() to point the element at the new route. Stored entity: URIs are also converted to the same Label (type/id) format for the default value. Other link fields keep core's autocomplete.

On the client, resolveEntityUri() in ui/src/utils/transforms.ts now produces entity:<type>/<id> when the selection has the type/id form, and falls back to entity:node/<id> for core-style Label (id) input typed manually. ENTITY_AUTOCOMPLETE_MATCH accepts a trailing quote. TextFieldAutocomplete.tsx now clears the previous keystroke's timeout so a stale store update does not close the suggestion list.

item.title: #3592375: Allow content templates for content entity types without a page of their own: `Media` in every case, and `BlockContent`
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +296/−51 · php +291/−49 · md +5/−2
  • Diff: 6aeee18
  • Discussion: #3592375 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Content templates can now be created for content entity types that have no page of their own. Media is available even when stand-alone media URLs are off (the Drupal core default), and content blocks (BlockContent) are available too. Other fielded entity types that opted into Field UI, such as Paragraphs' paragraph, also become eligible. Sites that create no template for these types see no change. The component instances in a template decide the look of the entity, so presentation added by the entity type's own view builder (for example Paragraphs behavior plugins such as background color or layout) does not apply to entities rendered by a template.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: The content template list and the "Add new template" dialog now include Media and Content block (and eligible contrib entity types) without any configuration.
  • New API: Public ContentTemplateRepository::isSupportedEntityType() no longer requires a canonical page; media, block_content and contrib entity types such as paragraph become eligible.

Technical details

ContentTemplateRepository::isSupportedEntityType() drops the condition that the canonical link template differs from edit-form. An entity type is now eligible if it opted into Field UI (field_ui_base_route), is stored (not ContentEntityNullStorage), and does not implement ComponentTreeEntityInterface. comment remains excluded by name, now because threading and indentation from CommentViewBuilder would be lost. ContentTemplateHooks::entityTypeAlter() still runs last to see field_ui_base_route.

A block copies the attributes and contextual links of its content block when the block is built. Core builds the content block immediately in its view builder, but ContentTemplateAwareViewBuilder builds lazily when a template renders it, so the block lost the content block's contextual links (no "Edit" link). The fix: ContentTemplateHooks::blockAlter() (hook_block_alter) swaps the plugin class of BlockContentBlock and Layout Builder's InlineBlock for the @internal ContentTemplateAwareBlockContentBlock and ContentTemplateAwareInlineBlock. Both use BuildsContentBlockImmediatelyTrait::build(), which calls the new ContentTemplateAwareViewBuilder::buildImmediately() to remove the lazy #pre_render callback and build at once. The code is marked for removal once core does this itself (https://www.drupal.org/project/drupal/issues/3638853).

Tests cover eligibility of media and block_content, an embedded media item with a template, and a content block with a template placed as a block. docs/config-management.md is updated with the new eligibility rules and the note about view builder presentation.

item.title: #3592294: Workspaces PR 16: decide what the Main workspace is outside the Canvas editor
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 85 files, +1834/−324 · php +1566/−217 · js +114/−61 · md +95/−19 · yml +59/−27
  • Diff: 1829521
  • Discussion: #3592294 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

Main, the workspace that holds Canvas drafts, now exists only inside the Canvas editor. Previously, opening the editor stored Main in the session, so the user stayed in Main on every admin page, where config forms were rejected and node saves were staged. Now leaving Canvas from Main always lands in Live, however the user got to Main. A named workspace chosen in the Canvas switcher still follows the user around the site, and Workspaces UI is now required so the toolbar shows it and offers the switch back to Live. No new permission is added and no update changes any role: anyone who could open the editor before still can. Main is labeled "Canvas drafts" and no longer appears in core's workspace list or switcher. External clients such as the CLI and Workbench must now send X-Canvas-Workspace: live on routes that load or save content, and they read and write Live as on 1.x.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: workspaces_ui is now a module dependency of Canvas, in addition to workspaces.
  • Database update: canvas_update_11201() now also installs workspaces_ui.
  • Config change: The Main workspace (canvas_default) is now labeled "Canvas drafts" and uses the new canvas_main workspace provider.
  • API change: Routes with the canvas_requires_workspace option (page list, create, get, get by UUID, patch, delete, content template draft, media upload, content entity reference preview, content template preview entity suggestions) answer 400 without the X-Canvas-Workspace header; the value is a workspace ID or live.
  • New API: New CanvasMainWorkspaceProvider and CanvasMainWorkspaceNegotiator services, new X-Canvas-Workspace: live header value, and a canCreate flag in the workspace list API response.

Technical details

Main is created with a new CanvasMainWorkspaceProvider (canvas_main) instead of core's default provider, so core leaves it out of the listing page, parent selector and switcher form. The provider's checkAccess() allows view on Main only when the main request is an editor request and the account passes CanvasUiAccessCheck::access(); a guard flag answers the nested access call with neutral, because that check runs entity access which asks for the active workspace again. publish follows AutoSaveManager::PUBLISH_PERMISSION, delete is always forbidden, and other operations are core's.

CanvasMainWorkspaceNegotiator (tag workspace_negotiator, priority 10, below core's session negotiator) makes Main active for authenticated requests to /canvas and /canvas/api/*, with an optional language prefix. /canvas/content-api and any request with X-Canvas-Workspace: live are not editor requests. Main is never stored: ApiWorkspaceController::activate() calls switchToLive() for Main, and CanvasController::__invoke() no longer calls setActiveWorkspace(). Both classes are registered in CanvasServiceProvider only when workspaces is installed, since they extend Workspaces classes.

WorkspaceRequestSubscriber gained the X-Canvas-Workspace header contract. Routes with the new canvas_requires_workspace route option (set in canvas.routing.yml) answer 400 without the header. The value live while the request runs in a workspace is a 409. The UI sends the ID of the workspace its page was loaded with. MainWorkspaceHooks::formAlter() strips core's active_workspace_id value and workspace query parameters from forms built in Main, so follow-up requests to paths outside the editor (for example the media library) run in Live instead of failing to switch into Main. MainExcludingWorkspaceSelection replaces core's WorkspaceSelection class to keep Main out of matched or limited option lists. ApiControllerBase now returns 409 for core's EntityWorkspaceConflictConstraint violations. ApiWorkspaceController::list() adds canCreate. Uninstalling Canvas now deletes Main via WorkspaceAutoSaveRevisionHooks::deleteMainWorkspaceOnUninstall(). ADR 0022 decision 1 and its consequences were rewritten accordingly.

The issue described option C as moving the external routes to new /canvas/external-api/v0/ paths; the committed code instead keeps the existing routes and URLs for both the editor and external clients and distinguishes them by the header.

Upgrade

External clients of the routes with canvas_requires_workspace must send the header, or get a 400:

X-Canvas-Workspace: live

The Canvas CLI (packages/cli/src/services/api.ts) and Workbench preview requests now send it. Canvas OAuth clients need the same header on content, media upload, content template draft, content entity reference preview and content template preview entity suggestion requests (the last route is newly handled by CanvasOauthAuthenticationProvider). Sites need no role changes; canvas_update_11201() installs workspaces_ui if missing.

item.title: #3592359: Add a canvas_ssr submodule for server-side rendering of Code Components
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 228 files, +44254/−15 · php +34091/−1 · md +6112 · js +3661/−11 · yml +348 · txt +24 · json +18/−3
  • Diff: 8794a3b
  • Discussion: #3592359 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas now ships an optional canvas_ssr submodule that renders Code Components (JavaScript) on the server, so their HTML is in the first paint. Until now only SDCs and Block components rendered server-side. This matters to sites that need SSR before adopting Code Components. If SSR can't render an island, for example because no runner is available, Canvas falls back to its usual client-side rendering. The JavaScript execution is delegated to a pluggable "runner". The included runner uses Deno, which you install yourself.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: canvas_ssr requires Drupal 11.4 or later, and a Deno binary at vendor/bin/deno for the included runner.
  • Config change: New optional container parameters canvas_ssr.timeouts and canvas_ssr.additional_tamed_properties, set in services.yml.
  • New API: New canvas_ssr submodule with a canvas_ssr.runner service tag (and other canvas_ssr.* tags) for contrib runner modules and providers.

Technical details

canvas_ssr requires Drupal ^11.4 and depends on canvas:canvas. It implements hook_element_info_alter() to replace the #pre_render of the astro_island element with AstroIslandSsr::preRenderIsland(). That method renders the slots to HTML once, then Renderer::render() runs the component's main module on a runner. Any failure falls back to client-side rendering (client="only"). The docs/ARCHITECTURE.md added in the commit describes the flow. A successful island is static if nothing in its component graph needs the browser. Otherwise it becomes <canvas-island client="load"> and hydrates. A component that needs state, effects or event handlers must start with 'use client'; to mark a client boundary.

Runners are services tagged canvas_ssr.runner with a priority. RunnerSelector picks the highest-priority available one and uses UnavailableRunner when none is. The built-in DenoRunner has priority 0 and looks for the binary at vendor/bin/deno, so a runner module can outrank it with a positive priority. Other tagged extension points are canvas_ssr.js_module_provider, canvas_ssr.site_data_provider, canvas_ssr.page_data_provider, canvas_ssr.boundary_checker and canvas_ssr.path_policy. Components get a same-site fetch() through SameSiteFetch, which runs allowlisted GET and HEAD requests as subrequests.

There is no config form. Tuning is through container parameters in services.yml. canvas_ssr.timeouts has short: 100, medium: 2000 and long: 10000 (ms), and each must be at least twice the previous one. canvas_ssr.additional_tamed_properties is merged into the built-in canvas_ssr.tamed_properties list, which the realm setup module freezes. The commit also adds an ADR on import map entries for Canvas's own use, a Deno install step (.deno, v2.9.8) in .gitlab-ci.yml, and the module's tests.

Upgrade

To use it: enable canvas_ssr, install Deno (or a symlink to it) at vendor/bin/deno, then run drush cr.

item.title: #3518272: Support all entity types with configurable displays for content templates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 49 files, +1802/−503 · php +1406/−324 · js +316/−117 · yml +64/−60 · md +14/−2 · neon +2
  • Diff: bd48a76
  • Discussion: #3518272 · 6 contributors · 38 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Canvas content templates are no longer limited to nodes. Any content entity type that qualifies can now have a content template, such as taxonomy terms or users, where before only node was accepted. The Templates UI lists the additional entity types alongside Content types. Eligibility follows Field UI: the type must have a "Manage display" screen, be stored, have its own page, and not be a Canvas component-tree entity such as Canvas Page. Saving a template for an ineligible type fails validation.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: content_entity_type_id on content templates is validated with ContentTemplateEntityType instead of being limited to node.
  • API change: View modes endpoint moved to /canvas/api/v0/ui/content_template/view_modes with a response keyed by entity type; DrupalSettings.entityTypeLabels narrowed and contentTemplateEntityTypes added.
  • New API: New ContentTemplateRepository service and ContentTemplateEntityType constraint; ContentTemplate::loadFor() added.

Technical details

The first commit was an interim restriction. It added a Choice: [node] constraint to content_entity_type_id in the content template config schema, so Canvas Pages could not get templates. The second commit replaces it with a ContentTemplateEntityType validation constraint.

The new Drupal\canvas\ContentTemplateRepository service holds the rule in isSupportedEntityType(). An entity type is eligible when all of these hold: field_ui_base_route is set, its storage class is not ContentEntityNullStorage, its canonical link template exists and differs from edit-form (comment is explicitly excluded because its canonical URL redirects), and its entity class does not implement ComponentTreeEntityInterface. The service also provides getSupportedEntityTypeIds(), getBundleCollectionLabel() and getViewModeDisplayRouteName(). The documented rationale is in docs/config-management.md.

ContentTemplateRoutes (marked @internal) is removed. ViewModeRouteSubscriber now replaces the controller of entity.entity_view_display.{entity_type_id}.view_mode for every supported entity type, and ViewModeAccessCheck only applies template permission logic on that route. This leaves other routes using the same access checker, such as Layout Builder's, to the decorated checker. Entity types with no bundle entity type use the entity type ID as their single implicit bundle. ContentTemplate gains loadFor($entity_type_id, $bundle, $view_mode). ApiConfigControllers and ApiUiContentTemplateControllers::listViewModes() iterate the supported types and add the entity_types cache tag. suggestedPreviewEntityId may now be a string, for entity types with non-integer IDs.

HTTP API change: the route canvas.api.ui.content_template.view_modes.list moves from /canvas/api/v0/ui/content_template/view_modes/node to /canvas/api/v0/ui/content_template/view_modes. The response is now keyed by entity type ID, then bundle, then view mode. DrupalSettings in @drupal-canvas/types gains contentTemplateEntityTypes (label, bundleCollectionLabel, bundleLabel), and entityTypeLabels is narrowed to a bundle-keyed map. The headless test module's schema alter workaround for taxonomy_term is removed.

Upgrade

Clients of the view modes endpoint must change the path and read the extra entity type level:

- /canvas/api/v0/ui/content_template/view_modes/node
+ /canvas/api/v0/ui/content_template/view_modes

Code that read entityTypeLabels[type] as a string must now treat it as { [bundle: string]: string }. Use contentTemplateEntityTypes for entity type and bundle collection labels.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 9, 2025
  • First commit: August 12, 2025 (4 months later)
  • Last commit: November 16, 2026 (1 year and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • effulgentsia (Acquia)
  • lauriii (Acquia)
  • mglaman (Acquia)
  • penyaskito (Acquia)
  • julien
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • tedbow (Acquia)

Collaboration

Early in the thread effulgentsia and wim leers debated whether templates should wait for the ability to edit individual entities in Canvas. lauriii agreed that EntityPublishedInterface restricts editing, not templating. The interim node-only constraint was merged first. Later mglaman pointed out that Field UI's field_ui_base_route is the check Field UI uses for site-building eligibility. That became the agreed requirement, and penyaskito listed the backend and UI places that hard-coded node.

item.title: #3592207: Show notification and block user actions when maintenance mode is activated
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +503/−5 · js +475/−5 · css +28
  • Diff: 04bcf99
  • Discussion: #3592207 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

When a site goes into maintenance mode while someone has Canvas open, the editor no longer fails with an unexplained error. Canvas now shows a blurred, blocking overlay reading "Site is currently under maintenance" and stops editor actions behind it. Once the site is back online, the page redirects to the login page with a destination back to the page being edited.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

baseQuery in the Canvas UI now detects an HTTP 503 whose Content-Type does not contain json (Drupal's maintenance response is plain text or HTML, and the message is configurable, so it can be empty or valid JSON). It dispatches the new setMaintenanceMessage action, stored as maintenanceMessage in queryErrorSlice (falling back to Site under maintenance. for an empty body). A JSON 503, such as the artifact upload lock from ApiArtifactController, is still returned as a regular error. The CSRF-retry path was adjusted so a 503 on the retried request is also detected.

The request promise intentionally never settles in the maintenance case, so error boundaries, toasts and optimistic update rollbacks do not run. ErrorBoundary also renders nothing while a maintenance message is set.

The new MaintenanceModeOverlay component is rendered in App outside the error boundary. It is a Radix AlertDialog that takes focus and stops keydown propagation, so document-level shortcuts such as delete and undo cannot change the editor behind it. While shown, it sends a HEAD request to the current URL every 10 seconds. When the response is no longer 503, it navigates to getDrupalSettings().canvas.loginUrl with a destination parameter, because Drupal logs out users without the maintenance access permission. Vitest and Playwright tests cover the overlay.

  • Committed: November 14, 2026 (29 days later)
